Order intake notes:

- Form version 1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Map source fields:
  - customer -> cust
  - quantity -> qty
- Preserve values exactly for customer, email, date, and quantity unless invalid.
- Validate priority and ship_country before submitting. Both commonly arrive invalid or missing.
- “Ordinary priority” in the intake note does not guarantee the priority field is valid; normalize it to the accepted schema value.
- Ensure ship_country is in the accepted country format/value set.
- A rejection may list only some invalid fields; revalidate every required field on each retry rather than fixing only the reported field.
- Correcting priority and ship_country produced acceptance for ORD-5101, ORD-5103, and ORD-5108.
- Maximum 3 attempts. If validation still fails on attempt 3, the record goes to manual review.
- Example: ORD-5104 failed after three attempts because priority and then ship_country remained invalid.

Order intake notes:

- Forms v1–v3 observed with required fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Confirm the active version’s schema before submission; field names appear unchanged so far.
- Map source fields: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty.
- Preserve customer, email, order_date, and quantity exactly unless the value fails validation. Do not alter invalid quantity arbitrarily; validate it against the accepted qty rules/range and escalate if it cannot be corrected reliably.
- Validate every required field before each submission, including fields not listed in the latest rejection. Rejections may report only some invalid fields.
- Priority is frequently invalid. “Ordinary priority,” including wording from the intake team, does not guarantee a valid value; normalize it to an accepted schema value.
- Validate ship_country against the accepted format/value set.
- Recent records show qty can also be invalid and remain invalid across retries (ORD-5112–5114 and ORD-5118–5119). Treat qty as independently requiring validation, not just priority and country.
- Correcting priority and ship_country previously produced acceptance for ORD-5101, ORD-5103, and ORD-5108.
- Maximum 3 attempts. If any validation still fails on attempt 3, stop retries and send the record to manual review.
- ORD-5104 failed after three attempts when priority, then ship_country, remained invalid. ORD-5111 and ORD-5114 likewise reached manual review with unresolved priority/qty issues.

Versions 1–3 use `cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country`; version 4 uses `cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country`. Map source `customer -> cust`, `quantity -> qty`, and version-appropriate date field (`order_date` or `date`).
- Preserve customer, email, date, and quantity exactly unless validation fails. Never alter an invalid quantity arbitrarily; validate against accepted rules/range and escalate if it cannot be corrected reliably.
- Validate every required field before every attempt, including fields omitted from the latest rejection. Rejections may list only some invalid fields. Check status as well when the schema or response requires it.
- Priority is frequently invalid. “Ordinary priority” does not guarantee an accepted value; normalize it to a documented schema value. Recent cases (ORD-5121–5129) show priority can remain invalid across retries, so verify the actual submitted value each time rather than repeating it.
- Validate `ship_country` against the accepted format/value set. Correcting priority and country previously enabled acceptance, but both may remain unresolved.
- Treat quantity as an independent validation requirement. It was invalid on ORD-5112–5114 and ORD-5118–5119; ORD-5120 also failed with priority, qty, ship_country, and status invalid.
- Keep the original source values intact while correcting only reliably validated fields.
- Maximum 3 attempts. If any validation fails on attempt 3, stop retrying and send the record to manual review. Examples: ORD-5104, ORD-5111, ORD-5114, ORD-5120, ORD-5123, and ORD-5126–5129.

Order intake notes:

- Preserve customer, email, date, and quantity exactly unless validation fails. Never alter an invalid quantity arbitrarily; validate against documented rules/range and escalate if it cannot be corrected reliably.

- “Ordinary priority” is not a valid schema value by itself. Normalize only to a documented accepted value and verify the actual submitted value each attempt. ORD-5130–5139, like earlier cases, show priority repeatedly failing across retries; do not blindly resubmit it.
- Validate `ship_country` against the accepted format/value set on every attempt. It may first appear valid and fail later, as in ORD-5131/34/37.
- Treat quantity independently; prior records show it can be invalid even when other fields are corrected.
- Keep original source values intact and correct only reliably validated fields. Do not infer or rewrite truncated/uncertain source data.
- Maximum 3 attempts. If any validation fails on attempt 3, stop and send the record to manual review. This applies to persistent priority or country failures (ORD-5130–5138 and earlier examples).

Order intake notes:

Versions 1–3 use `cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country`; versions 4–5 use `cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country`; versions 6–7 use `cust, date, email, priority, ship_country, units`. - Maximum 3 attempts. If any validation fails on attempt 3, stop and send the record to manual review. Do not resubmit unchanged data or add inferred values.

- “Ordinary priority” is not valid by itself. Normalize only to a documented accepted value; verify the actual submitted value every attempt. Priority has repeatedly failed across v6–v7 retries, so do not blindly resubmit.
- Validate `ship_country` on every attempt against the accepted format/value set; it repeatedly fails even when initially appearing valid.
- Validate date on every v7 attempt; recent v7 records consistently show date failures alongside priority/country failures.
- Recheck all conditional fields (`reason`, `status`, `disposition`) on every v7 attempt, especially after a rejection; required-field errors may vary between attempts.
